feedback.problem: Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix such that $\text{tr}(A)=-14$ and $\text{det}(A)=-36.$ Then, ${A}^{2}=$
feedback.worked_solution:
The characteristic polynomial of $A$ is given by 

$$
p(\lambda )={\lambda }^{2}-\text{tr}(A)\lambda +\text{det}(A).
$$

Therefore, using the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p(A) & =O \\ {A}^{2}-\text{tr}(A)A+\text{det}(A)I & =O \\ {A}^{2} & =\text{tr}(A)A-\text{det}(A)I \\ {A}^{2} & =-14A+36I.\end{aligned}
$$
